clue.text: Change one's bank, perhaps

parts.note: the surface suggests switching to another lender, but the bank is a river bank you move from to the far side

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about moving their account to a different high-street lender.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'bank' is not a financial institution but the side of a river; getting to the other side is the act described.
explanation.definitionFit: Going across from one river edge to the opposite one is a literal passage to the other side.

clue.text: Stop firm acquiring half the capital of England

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company, a firm

indicators.note: half says only the first half of the word is used

parts.note: London is the capital of England

explanation.surface: A company bids to buy half of London.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the first half of LONDON, LON, is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A colon is a punctuation mark, a stop in old printers' terms.

clue.text: An individual with sour disposition is hard to bear

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: disposition read as arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sour-tempered person is difficult to put up with.
explanation.definitionFit: Something burdensome or oppressive is difficult to carry or endure.

clue.text: Smooth look about a novice

indicators.note: the word for look goes round the learner letter

parts.note: to seek is to look for
L is a learner, from the L-plate on a learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A beginner has a polished appearance.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy and streamlined describes something with a smooth surface.

clue.text: Remarkable novel, it is intensely passionate

indicators.note: read as re-markable, these letters can be marked out anew in another order

explanation.surface: A book reviewer praises a remarkable and intensely passionate new novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Extreme or fierce feelings are violent in their intensity.

clue.text: Check power increase

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
force means power

explanation.surface: An instruction to verify that power is increasing.
explanation.definitionFit: To strengthen something by adding to it is to boost or increase it.

clue.text: An overcrowded children's home in Oxford, say

definitions.meaning: the nursery-rhyme old woman lived in one and had so many children she didn't know what to do
an Oxford is a style of laced leather footwear

explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'There was an old woman who lived in a shoe' is well known in Britain; 'Oxford' is the footwear, not the city.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme's crowded dwelling and the laced Oxford are both items of footwear.

clue.text: A good man helped to put it on the map

definitions.text: A good man helped to put it on the map

parts.words: A good man helped to put it on the map
parts.note: the Good Samaritan's parable made his homeland region famous

explanation.surface: A kindly person helped make a place famous.
explanation.walkthrough: The Good Samaritan of Jesus's parable came from this ancient region of Palestine.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical region was home to the Samaritans, made famous by the parable.

clue.text: At risk when making a call

definitions.meaning: in jeopardy, like a reputation staked
a telephone caller is connected on the phone

explanation.definitionFit: Being in danger and being in a phone conversation are both described by this idiom.

clue.text: Get a role as someone's double

definitions.text: Get a role as someone's double

parts.words: Get a role as someone's double
parts.note: an actor cast to play a person's other self has a part as their second identity; the letters of 'get a role' also rearrange to the answer

explanation.surface: An actor lands a part playing a stand-in or lookalike.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of 'Get a role' rearrange to the answer, but no word signals the shuffle, so the clue works as a cryptic definition with an anagram bonus.
explanation.definitionFit: A second self or alternative personality is a person's double in a figurative sense.

clue.text: The occupant is at home with his wife

parts.note: in means at home, as in 'staying in'
a mate is a spouse or partner

explanation.surface: A householder is described as being in the house with his spouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A prisoner or resident of an institution is someone occupying a place there.

clue.text: Free admittance?

parts.note: read 'free' as a verb: to release a means of entry, such as a door

explanation.surface: A sign advertises that entry costs nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Free' looks like an adjective meaning no charge; read it as a verb, to open the way in.
explanation.definitionFit: Releasing a lock allows entry, freeing the way to be admitted.

clue.text: Compelled to use pressure in extremity

indicators.note: the pressure word is placed inside the word for extremity

parts.note: an end is an extremity
force means pressure

explanation.surface: Someone resorts to pressure when pushed to the limit.
explanation.definitionFit: Something compelled was made to happen by force, imposed rather than voluntary.

clue.text: Succeeded in exam in oral history

indicators.note: an oral is spoken, so the word for history is heard rather than written

parts.note: the past is history

explanation.surface: A student did well in a spoken history examination.
explanation.definitionFit: To get through a test successfully is to have made the grade in it.

clue.text: Doctor meant to go round some accommodation

indicators.note: the rearranged letters surround the word for some
to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered

parts.note: a part is some of something

explanation.surface: A physician intended to visit some lodgings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a physician but is the anagram signal; 'to go round' says the shuffled letters surround the piece for 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat is a set of rooms forming living accommodation.

clue.text: Where the fare goes down as the journey lengthens

definitions.text: Where the fare goes down as the journey lengthens

parts.words: Where the fare goes down as the journey lengthens
parts.note: fare is food, eaten in a railway carriage while the trip continues

explanation.surface: A ticket price that falls the further you travel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fare' suggests a ticket price going down; it is food going down throats on the train.
explanation.definitionFit: A railway carriage serving meals is where passengers eat while travelling.

clue.text: Reptile bringing back one young salmon in ten

indicators.note: the reversed pieces sit inside the word for ten
the one and the young salmon are read backwards

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a parr is a young salmon

explanation.surface: A reptile is returning a small salmon in a group of ten.
explanation.walkthrough: A parr is a young salmon, a word solvers may not know; 'bringing back' turns only the one and the salmon, which then sit inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: A freshwater turtle is a reptile.

clue.text: Grand occasion, of course

parts.note: the Grand ... is a big steeplechase run on the Aintree racecourse

explanation.surface: A major event, naturally.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grand National is Britain's famous steeplechase at Aintree; 'of course' means on a racecourse, not 'naturally'.
explanation.definitionFit: The second word of the famous Grand steeplechase names the race on its course.

clue.text: Disturbed, a newt is agitated

indicators.note: agitated means stirred up, so these letters are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: An amphibian is upset and agitated.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious and flustered is an idiom for being in a state of worry.

clue.text: Siren indicating danger on the Rhine

definitions.meaning: a siren is a seductive water spirit luring sailors to doom
the rock of that name on the river is a notorious navigational hazard

explanation.walkthrough: The Lorelei legend tells of a maiden on a Rhine rock whose song wrecked boatmen.
explanation.definitionFit: The German legend's enchantress and the perilous river rock share the name.

clue.text: He's mastered the art of eating out

definitions.text: He's mastered the art of eating out

parts.words: He's mastered the art of eating out
parts.note: an engraver uses acid to eat lines out of a metal plate

explanation.surface: A man has become an expert at dining in restaurants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eating out' suggests restaurants; it is the acid biting into a printing plate.
explanation.definitionFit: A printmaker who uses acid to bite designs into metal practises this art.

clue.text: Crafty boxer?

definitions.meaning: read as 'a craft', a kind of boat such as a motor yacht with cabins
a fighter in the weight division between light-heavyweight and heavyweight

explanation.walkthrough: 'Crafty' means of a craft (a vessel), not cunning; a cruiserweight boxes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pleasure boat or warship and a boxing weight division both carry this name.

clue.text: One who tries hard to get a riddle?

definitions.meaning: someone who strains is making a great effort
a riddle is a coarse sieve, a device for sifting

explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddle' means a sieve here, not a puzzle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sieve filters, and a person who exerts great effort strains.

clue.text: Those in the majority

parts.note: majority is the age of legal adulthood, so these are people who have reached it

explanation.surface: The people on the winning side of a vote.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Majority' means coming of age, not the larger group.
explanation.definitionFit: Grown-ups are people who have attained the legal age of full responsibility.

clue.text: Mob dispersed, when sailor is about to produce weapon

indicators.note: the sailor letters surround the scattered mob

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

indicators.note: a crowd dispersed is broken up, so these letters are scattered

explanation.surface: A crowd scatters as a sailor prepares to make a weapon.
explanation.definitionFit: An atomic bomb is a nuclear weapon.

clue.text: Getting the short measure and taking offence

parts.note: ft is the abbreviation for a foot, a unit of measure

explanation.surface: Someone is cheated on quantity and feels insulted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking offence' looks like being upset; it is the offence of taking, stealing.
explanation.definitionFit: Stealing is the crime of taking property unlawfully.

clue.text: Cross one side of Glasgow

definitions.meaning: a ... cross is a ringed stone cross
... and Rangers are Glasgow's two rival football clubs

explanation.walkthrough: Celtic is one of Glasgow's two great football clubs, the other being Rangers.
explanation.definitionFit: The ringed Irish-style monument and the Glasgow football club share this name.

clue.text: Dangerous position, where pride goes before a retreat

indicators.note: the pride word is put ahead of the retreat word

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions
a den is a private retreat

explanation.surface: Arrogance leads one to seek a hiding place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pride goes before a fall' is the proverb the surface echoes; here pride is a group of big cats.
explanation.definitionFit: Being among hostile people is figuratively entering a place of great peril, as Daniel did.

clue.text: Cram for a sound public school

indicators.note: the school's name is heard, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: Stowe is a well-known English public school in Buckinghamshire

explanation.surface: Someone swots for a good private school.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a fee-paying English boarding school; 'Cram' suggests studying hard, but means pack.
explanation.definitionFit: To pack items tightly into a space is to stuff them away.

clue.text: Sudden downfall in Iran?

parts.note: Iran is what you get when the letters of rain are burst apart

explanation.surface: A regime suddenly collapses in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: read the answer as wordplay, rain broken up, and it gives Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: A short heavy shower is a sudden fall of water from the sky.
